To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
institutional structure and the way it was designed, as well as the historical paths of development, influence the outcome of reforms aimed at reducing the gender bias.

(i) the Swedish pension reform was based on the rational design, which was aimed at overcoming gender bias in the pension system; (ii) the Polish pension reform was based upon the institutional heritage, which resulted in the preservation of gender bias in the new pension system.

(1) pension reforms in Sweden and Poland have been designed to address gender inequality in old age security systems; (2) these reforms have been implemented in different social, cultural and institutional contexts; and (3) the outcomes of these reforms have differed in both countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutional approach to pension reforms and gender inequality in the context of Sweden and Poland.
the institutional approach to the problem of gender bias within pension systems and its outcomes.
institutional approach to gender bias in old age security systems and the role of institutional structure in the process of reforming these systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
institutions are not necessarily rational, but they are rational in the context of their sociocultural environment.
the institutional structure is a result of a complex interaction of rational design and sociocultural heritage.
the institutional structures of pension systems are the result of a combination of rational design and sociocultural factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the institutional structures of pension systems are the result of both rational design and sociocultural heritage.
institutional structures, which are the result of rational design, are not always able to overcome sociocultural heritage.
the institutional structure of pension systems in Poland and Sweden has been influenced by sociocultural heritage, and that this heritage has been more influential in Poland than Sweden.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same institution may produce different results in different social contexts and that these differences are not only a result of rational design but also of sociocultural factors.
gender related problems in the pension systems are not the outcome of rational choice.
the institutional approach allows for a better understanding of the processes of institutional change, especially in cases when the outcomes of institutional reforms are unexpected.
